text:
lina (Support): customer G-42 reports streaming completions getting cut off ~30s into the stream. client shows final chunk missing, then the client tries to reconnect and receives a 200 but no body. they see billing for resumed tokens which is confusing. :confused:

ajay (Eng Runtime): do we have any recent changes to sse keepalive / comment-ping behavior? any rollout to edge proxies?

lina (Support): not from customer side — they say it started after upgrading SDK to 0.9.2, but the repro also happens with curl.

dan (Eng SRE): saw similar alerts last week — spike in partial-stream reports from one region. I instrumented proxy logs, looked noisy connections dropped with FIN from client side after 30s of inactivity.

kevin (Product): billing-bot flagged a few resumed-stream invoices. customer expects not to be charged for duplicate/resumed tokens if no data flowed. can we confirm billing behavior on reconnect?

billing-bot: automated note: resumed stream sessions are billed for tokens generated after handshake is accepted; token dedupe is not performed across session restarts.

ajay (Eng Runtime): thanks. hypothesis: some clients rely on comment pings (SSE comments like `: heartbeat\n\n`) to keep browser connection alive. If an intermediary (ALB/nginx) drops TCP due to no data for 30s, the client might think server closed and then sends a new request using Last-Event-ID. The runtime accepts and replays but billing treats continuation as new generate. we need to detect dead connections earlier and send a very small event or explicit `: ping` that passes through proxies.

lina (Support): customer provided a curl repro, pasted below (redacted):

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-3x"
```

They say after ~30s no more events come even though server still generating. Client then reconnects with `Last-Event-ID: 12345`.

ajay (Eng Runtime): can you ask for a tcpdump from the client side capturing the FIN/RST? also need proxy access logs around the request id. if the proxy closes TCP there will be no TCP-level keepalive seen.

dan (Eng SRE): I pulled ALB logs for a sample request id — see snippet:

```
2026-02-18T14:23:01Z request_id=abc123 client_ip=1.2.3.4 elb_status=200 backend_status=200 idle_timeout=30
2026-02-18T14:23:31Z request_id=abc123 terminated_by=client reason=FIN
```

idle_timeout=30 stands out. our ALB default idle is 30s in that region. If a comment ping doesn't count as data, ALB might still consider the connection idle.

ajay (Eng Runtime): aha — many proxies treat lines starting with `:` as comments and still consider them bytes on the wire, but some middleboxes drop comments before counting toward idle. we should prefer sending small 1-byte event like `event: ping\ndata: \n\n` or an actual SSE `data: \n\n` payload at an interval < idle timeout (e.g., 15s).

kevin (Product): changing to 15s pings is fine product-wise, but we should also think about cost and client behaviour: will clients treat that as a real token? we must ensure pings are not counted against token usage and are stripped before billing.

ajay (Eng Runtime): pings are purely transport-layer events and should not be included in the model output pipeline. runtime currently emits comment pings from the compilation layer which are not routed through token accounting. but if we switch to `event: ping\ndata: \n\n` we must guarantee the token-metering code ignores `ping` events.

dan (Eng SRE): short-term mitigation: reduce ALB idle timeout to 60s? that helps but not ideal. long-term: explicit transport-level keepalive that intermediaries respect.

oncall: suggest enabling TCP keepalive on long-lived backends as well — some platforms use shorter OS-level TCP keepalive (e.g., 15s) so even if a proxy doesn't see data, TCP will still probe. downside: kernel-level keepalive intervals are coarse and may produce spurious probes.
notes: contains logs and code block, discussion of comment pings vs event pings, billing implications
